tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the README files to understand what Chaterm is: an AI-native terminal for infrastructure and cloud resource management, built on Electron 30 + Vue 3 + TypeScript. The English and Chinese READMEs establish the project's purpose (intelligent command completion, multi-device management, AI Agent, enterprise security) and frame the three-layer Electron architecture that the rest of the tour will walk through.

tour.title: Main Process Entry
tour.description: src/main/index.ts is the Electron main process entry: it bootstraps the app, registers IPC handlers, wires up window creation, database connections, agent services, and SSH subsystems. With 49 exports and 57 outgoing edges, it is the single most-connected file in the project — every major subsystem (storage, agent, SSH, k8s) is initialized here. Reading this file gives you the runtime map of the entire desktop application.

tour.title: Window Management
tour.description: The windowManager is responsible for creating and orchestrating BrowserWindow instances: the main terminal window, the login window, and any child windows. It coordinates with the preload bridge (Step 4) to set up secure contextIsolation, and is the layer that decides how renderer pages are loaded. Together with src/main/index.ts, it forms the skeleton the renderer process plugs into.

tour.title: Preload Bridge
tour.description: The preload layer is the only sanctioned channel between renderer and main. src/preload/index.ts uses contextBridge to expose a typed, minimal API surface (e.g. window.api.terminal.*) and src/preload/index.d.ts is the corresponding TypeScript contract that the renderer depends on. This is the security boundary of the application — renderer code never sees Node.js directly, only the surface the preload intentionally exposes.

tour.title: Renderer Entry & Routing
tour.description: src/renderer/src/main.ts mounts the Vue 3 application onto the DOM and wires Vue Router, Pinia, and Vue I18n. App.vue is the root component, and views/index.vue is the default landing view. The router configuration (routes.ts) and guards.ts define how the SPA navigates between terminal sessions, settings, agents, and plugin views. This is where the user-facing terminal experience begins.

tour.title: AI Agent Core Loop
tour.description: The agent's central nervous system lives under src/main/agent/core. The Controller class (core/controller/index.ts) orchestrates task lifecycles, while core/task/index.ts implements the streaming request loop: it sends messages to the model, parses tool-use blocks, dispatches to registered tools, and persists results. With 24 fan-in, core/task/index.ts is the most-reused file in the agent layer — every AI-driven feature routes through it.
tour.languageLesson: Async generator streams (async function*) are used throughout the agent loop: model tokens flow through one generator, tool execution flows through another, and the controller pumps them together. This composes the streaming + tool-use pattern without callback hell.

tour.title: AI Provider Adapters
tour.description: src/main/agent/api/index.ts is the provider factory: it inspects the user's model configuration and instantiates the right ApiHandler. The providers/ directory holds one adapter per vendor — Anthropic, OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, DeepSeek, Ollama, LiteLLM — each implementing a shared streaming interface. This is how the agent stays model-agnostic: swapping providers is a one-line config change, not a refactor.
tour.languageLesson: The ApiHandler interface is a discriminated union pattern: every provider implements the same createMessage(stream) method but produces different wire formats. TypeScript's structural typing means the controller never has to switch on provider type — the interface guarantees the contract.

tour.title: Agent Services & Tool Registry
tour.description: The services/ directory holds the agent's toolbox: file glob/grep, terminal interaction detection, telemetry, and the ExperienceManager that learns from past sessions. shared/api.ts defines the wire protocol between renderer and main (webview messages), and shared/WebviewMessage.ts validates the contract. This is where the agent grows new capabilities — adding a tool means registering it here, not in the controller.

tour.title: Storage & Database
tour.description: src/main/storage/db/connection.ts opens the better-sqlite3 databases and runs the migration system (idempotent migration files under db/migrations). chaterm.service.ts is the central facade that exposes every domain (assets, keychains, tasks, snippets) to the rest of the main process. The data_sync subsystem handles cloud synchronization with envelope encryption and conflict resolution. This is the source of truth for all persistent state.
tour.languageLesson: better-sqlite3 is synchronous, which sounds wrong for an event-loop-sensitive Electron main process, but it is actually the right choice: it avoids callback overhead for sub-millisecond queries, simplifies transactions, and the main process is not doing high-throughput I/O. Migrations are idempotent — they check system tables before applying, so a partially-applied migration is recoverable.

tour.title: SSH & Remote Networking
tour.description: The SSH layer is Chaterm's connection backbone. sshHandle.ts is the core connection manager (SOCKS5/HTTP proxy support, keyboard-interactive auth, port forwarding). agentHandle.ts is the agent-specific variant that detects the remote shell and injects agent commands. The jumpserver/ and mingyu-plugin/ subdirectories implement bastion-host plugins — pluggable navigation flows for the two most common Chinese enterprise bastions. capabilityRegistry.ts is the dispatcher that maps bastion type to its plugin.

tour.title: Plugin System
tour.description: src/main/plugin/ is the extension system that lets users add new bastion types, commands, or UI panels without forking Chaterm. pluginManager.ts is the lifecycle owner (load/unload, registration); pluginLoader.ts handles dynamic imports of plugin modules in a sandboxed context. The renderer counterpart lives in src/renderer/src/api/plugin/plugin.ts and src/renderer/src/views/components/Extensions/. This is the seam where the project becomes extensible.

tour.title: i18n & Internationalization
tour.description: Chaterm ships with ten language locales (English, Simplified/Traditional Chinese, Japanese, Korean, German, French, Italian, Portuguese, Russian, Arabic). src/renderer/src/locales/index.ts bootstraps the i18n instance and the lang/ directory holds each language file. The agent itself is also bilingual: src/main/agent/core/prompts/system.ts and responses.ts contain the SYSTEM_PROMPT in both English and Chinese, so model behavior adapts to the user's language.

tour.title: Build, Package & CI/CD
tour.description: electron.vite.config.ts wires the build for all three Electron processes (main, preload, renderer) and configures the path aliases (@core, @services, @api, @shared). electron-builder.yml and the cn/global variants define how the app gets packaged into Windows / macOS / Linux installers. The .github/workflows/ pipelines run tests, security scans, and codeql analysis on every PR. Together these files turn source code into a distributable desktop binary.
tour.languageLesson: electron-vite is to Electron what Vite is to the web: separate dev servers per process, but a single Vite-aware bundler. The envPrefix: 'RENDERER_' guard on the renderer config means the renderer can only read variables explicitly prefixed that way — everything else is filtered out before preload contextBridge, which is a defense-in-depth measure on top of contextIsolation.
